notes: Curated for BrainDump Lite: instruct models that answer directly (no thinking phase) and follow JSON schemas. Every architecture is supported by the app's pinned llama.cpp build; file hashes and sizes are checked against Hugging Face. vram_gb is the smallest GPU that runs the model fully on-GPU at the app's 8K context; ram_gb is what a CPU-only run needs; both come from one size-based formula and are estimates. Nothing here downloads until the user picks it.

chat_models.label: Llama 3.2 3B
chat_models.blurb: Light and quick — for 4 GB cards or CPU-only machines
caveats: Smallest model here: best for quick, simple dumps. Long dumps get less nuanced extraction.
Llama community license (attribution required; not an OSI open-source license).

chat_models.label: Qwen3 4B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Best quality for its size — the sweet spot for 6 GB cards
caveats: The Instruct-2507 edition answers directly, with no thinking phase.

chat_models.label: Gemma 3 4B
chat_models.blurb: Google's small model — warmer writing voice
caveats: Multimodal model; only text is used here.
Gemma's terms of use apply (not a standard open-source license).

chat_models.label: Llama 3.1 8B
chat_models.blurb: The biggest here — needs a full 8 GB card
caveats: Llama community license (attribution required; not an OSI open-source license).

chat_models.label: Ministral 3 3B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Mistral's smallest current model — light, with a long context window
caveats: Vision-capable model, but BrainDump Lite only uses its text side.

chat_models.label: Granite 4.1 3B
chat_models.blurb: IBM's small business-tuned model — steady, plain-spoken output
caveats: Tuned for enterprise tasks such as extraction and tool use, so reflections may read more clinical than chatty.

chat_models.label: Phi-4 mini
chat_models.blurb: Microsoft's compact reasoner — strong on logic, less on warmth
caveats: Primarily trained on English; weaker in other languages.
Leans toward logic and math over warm, conversational replies.

chat_models.label: Gemma 4 E2B
chat_models.blurb: Google's newest small model — light to run
caveats: The "E" means effective: the file holds more parameters than the 2B in the name, so it is bigger than a true 2B model.
Multimodal model; only text is used here.

chat_models.label: Gemma 4 E4B
chat_models.blurb: Google's newer small model — a step up from Gemma 3 4B
caveats: The "E" means effective: the file holds more parameters than the 4B in the name, so it is bigger than a true 4B model.
Multimodal model; only text is used here.

chat_models.label: Ministral 3 8B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Mistral's mid-size model — a capable all-rounder with a very long context window
caveats: Vision-capable model, but BrainDump Lite only uses its text side.

chat_models.label: Granite 4.1 8B
chat_models.blurb: IBM's 8B — built for structured, business-style output
caveats: Tuned for enterprise tasks such as extraction and tool use, so reflections may read more clinical than chatty.

chat_models.label: Olmo 3 7B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Fully open model from Ai2 — training data and code are public too
caveats: English-focused.

chat_models.label: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Previous-generation Qwen — proven, predictable, strong multilingual
caveats: 2024 release; newer models here usually beat it, but it never spends tokens thinking out loud.

chat_models.label: Gemma 4 12B
chat_models.blurb: Google's 12B — a step up from the 4B class, with Gemma's warmer voice
caveats: Multimodal model; only text is used here.

chat_models.label: Ministral 3 14B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: The largest Ministral — long context, multilingual
caveats: Vision-capable model, but BrainDump Lite only uses its text side.

chat_models.label: Qwen2.5 14B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Previous-generation Qwen at 14B — proven, predictable, strong multilingual
caveats: 2024 release; newer models here usually beat it, but it never spends tokens thinking out loud.
Slow if it has to run on the CPU.

chat_models.label: Phi-4 14B
chat_models.blurb: Microsoft's 14B — reasoning-focused, English-first
caveats: Primarily trained on English; weaker in other languages.
Slow if it has to run on the CPU.

chat_models.label: Mistral Small 3.2 24B
chat_models.blurb: Mistral's 24B in a smaller quant so it fits 16 GB cards
caveats: IQ4_XS is a smaller quantization chosen to fit 16 GB; expect slightly lower fidelity than Q4_K_M.
Dense 24B: slow if it has to run on the CPU.
Vision-capable model, but BrainDump Lite only uses its text side.

chat_models.label: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
chat_models.blurb: Google's mixture-of-experts — a big model's knowledge at small-model speed
caveats: Mixture-of-experts: only about 4B parameters run per token so it is fast, but every weight must still fit in memory.
Multimodal model; only text is used here.

chat_models.label: Qwen3 30B-A3B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Big Qwen mixture-of-experts — a big model's knowledge at small-model speed
caveats: Mixture-of-experts: only about 3B parameters run per token so it is fast, but every weight must still fit in memory.
The 2507 Instruct edition answers directly, with no thinking phase.

chat_models.label: Gemma 4 31B
chat_models.blurb: Google's largest Gemma — big-model quality with Gemma's warmer voice
caveats: Dense 31B: noticeably slower than the mixture-of-experts models of similar size.
Multimodal model; only text is used here.

chat_models.label: Olmo 3.1 32B Instruct
chat_models.blurb: Largest fully open model here — training data and code are public
caveats: Dense 32B: slow unless it fits fully in VRAM.
English-focused.
